notes.yambala: Ruk is to put on or wear.
notes.yambula: Lony is to take off or untie.

guidebook.intro: **Bongo** means clothes. Learn to dress, undress and buy something new.

tips.title: Ruk and lony
body: **Ruk** is put on and **lony** take off: **Ruk cweta** (put on a sweater), **Lony war megi** (take off your shoes). **Aruko** is “I wear” and **Atye ka ruko** “I am putting on”.
Shoes are many, so “your” is **megi**: **war megi**. One shirt takes **meri**: **cati meri**.

tips.title: Too big, too small
body: **Dit** (big) and **tidi** (small) with **matek** (strongly) mean too much: **Kalacal bor matek** (the trousers are too long). When something fits, say **Romo koma** (it fits my body).

culture.title: Dressing up
body: For church, weddings and the **kwanjula** women often wear the **gomesi** and men a **kanju** with a jacket. Many Acholi women also tie a bright **kanga** over their clothes for work and dance.
